# Coronium Reseller Kit

Open-source starter kit for building a mobile-proxy reseller dashboard on top of the Coronium API (<https://dashboard.coronium.io>).

## What this is for

You (the LLM agent) are scaffolding a proxy reseller business for someone. They sell Coronium's mobile 4G/5G proxies to their end-customers with markup. This repo gives you the pattern, examples, and exact API surface to do it in one shot.

## Where to start reading

1. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/AGENTS.md> - your instructions
2. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/PROMPT.md> - the prompts the human will paste
3. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/docs/billing-and-reconciliation.md> - charged amount, coupon before/after, carrier, webhook receipt
4. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/docs/feature-badges.md> - IPv6, p0f and OpenVPN badges: which field, when to show, what a buy can guarantee
4. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/docs/p0f-and-openvpn.md> - p0f stock per region, `require: ["p0f"]`, OpenVPN download answers
4. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/docs/ipv6-lines.md> - Picking IPv6 lines: `ipv6_count`, `require: ["ipv6"]`, `409 ipv6_unavailable`, replacement, what IPv6 does and does not guarantee
5. <https://github.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/tree/main/examples/nextjs-dashboard> - working foundation
6. <https://api.coronium.io/openapi.json> - public REST specification, also rendered at <https://api.coronium.io/api-docs/>.
7. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/CHANGELOG.md> - dated API and kit changes, breaking vs additive
8. <https://github.com/coroniumio/coronium-proxy-mcp#agents-without-a-browser> - the MCP server (`npx -y coronium-proxy-mcp@2.4.3`; hosted `https://api.coronium.io/mcp`, 22 tools, never spends, and `https://api.coronium.io/mcp/buyer`, 15 tools, 20 when purchases are allowed) and the no-browser sign-up and funding walk-through
9. <https://dashboard.coronium.io/en/agents> - copyable agent setup prompts (API key, MCP, SDK, REST, Stripe MPP)

## Stripe Link wallet checkout

[MPP buyer guide](https://www.coronium.io/blog/buy-a-mobile-proxy-with-stripe-mpp) and [step-by-step buyer script](https://www.coronium.io/.well-known/agent-skills/coronium-mpp-checkout/SKILL.md). `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/mpp` with `{tariff_id, currency: "usd", max_total_usd}`, `Content-Type: application/json` (anything else answers `415`) and an `Idempotency-Key` quotes one eligible dedicated rental in USD: HTTP 402 with a `WWW-Authenticate: Payment` challenge (amount in cents, five minutes), nothing charged. Keep the buyer’s Coronium Bearer in `Authorization`. After the buyer approves the exact offer, send the wallet credential in `Payment-Authorization` with the same body bytes, credential preference and idempotency key. Follow the original status URL on the Coronium API origin until it shows `status: completed` with the line in `modems`. Only some dedicated plans can be bought this way, and the catalog does not mark them. Terms are daily, weekly or monthly, and p0f is not offered on this checkout. `require: ["ipv6"]` answers `409 ipv6_unavailable` there before any quote or charge: buy IPv6 lines on another lane. A plan it cannot fill answers `409` with code `spt_stock_unavailable`; on the first request that charges nothing, so pick another plan or pay from account credit. Buyer wallet: `npm install -g @stripe/link-cli@1.6.0`, `link-cli auth login`, `link-cli mpp decode --challenge`, `link-cli mpp pay` (it adds `Payment-Authorization` itself; its output repeats the request headers, so keep it private). Link agent wallets are for US and Canadian Link accounts for now. A buyer-approved shared payment token pays the same rental through `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/buy-with-shared-payment-token`. `POST /payment/mpp` is listed in the OpenAPI from version 3.3.17.

## Native IPv6

Native IPv6 means the line reaches IPv6-only sites over its own mobile IPv6 address. What we guarantee: every line sold with `require: ["ipv6"]` passed that check through its own proxy port within the last 2 hours, and is checked again just before it is handed over when that check is more than 10 minutes old. What we cannot guarantee: the mobile carrier assigns the IPv6 address per session, so a rotation, restart or reconnect gives the line a new address, and whether it gets IPv6 again is the carrier's decision, not ours; we do not re-check sold lines on a schedule. Sites that offer both IPv4 and IPv6 may still be reached over IPv4. We have not verified OS fingerprint (p0f) control on IPv6 connections. Replacement honours the requirement: `/replace` on a line bought with `require: ["ipv6"]` gives a line with a fresh IPv6 check, or answers `409 ipv6_replacement_unavailable` and changes nothing. A paid order whose free lines all fail that final check waits as a delayed order until a line passes it; it is never filled with a line without IPv6.

## API endpoints you'll use

- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/proxies` - list owned proxies
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account` - account credit, BTC and USDT balances
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/signup` `{login, password, name, purpose?}`, then `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/get-token` `{login, password}` (plus `code`, the current two-factor code, when the account has two-factor login), then `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v1/account/api-token` with that session token as Bearer - an agent opens its own account and gets the 365-day API key (`{token, expiresAt}`). Disposable and reserved email domains (including `.test`, `.example`, `.invalid`, `.localhost`) are refused; sign-ups are limited per IP address (5 accounts a day) and per uncommon email domain (5 an hour); a verification email is sent and nothing waits for it. The account starts empty: nothing is included until paid
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/crypto-balance` - USDT (TRC-20) and BTC deposit addresses and balances, plus account credit (an array with `coin` `btc`, `usdt`, `account_credit`). The first call creates missing deposit wallets
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/balance/convert` - move the account's own confirmed USDT and/or BTC into USD account credit, one way (BTC at the live rate, USDT 1:1). Body `{coin: "usdt", "btc" or "all" (default), amount_usd (number >= 1, single coin only), dry_run: true to preview}`. A real move needs an `Idempotency-Key` header (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}`). `200` `data` = `{moved: [{coin, coin_amount, usd, rate, move_id, status, replay}], refused, account_credit_before, account_credit_after}`; `409` when nothing moved (`nothing_to_move` under $1 with `coin: "all"`, or per-coin `refused` codes such as `NOTHING_TO_MOVE` or `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`). A key with `.` or `:`, or longer than 128 characters, answers `400` "Invalid Idempotency-Key format"
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/card-list`, `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/buy-with-card/{card_id}`, `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renew-with-card/{card_id}` - saved cards. A person adds the card in the dashboard (Stripe). Same body as the balance lanes; a declined card or one that needs authentication answers `402`, nothing charged
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/proxies/health` - per-proxy liveness; automate on `health.state` (`ok`, `degraded`, `down`, `unknown`) and `health.checked_at`
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/tariffs/available` - in-stock tariffs with `features.p0f.count`, `features.openvpn.count` and (OpenAPI 3.3.18) `features.ipv6.count`, equal to `ip_stack.ipv6` (public, no auth - use it to smoke-test connectivity)
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/free-modems?country_id=*` - stock per country, carrier and region, each row with `p0f_count` (public). Since OpenAPI 3.3.16 each row also has `openvpn_count`, `ipv6_count` and `one_time_only_count`, and since 3.3.18 `p0f_ipv6_count` (integers, always present, never more than `count`), plus `dataAllowanceNote` `{gbPerMonth, text, count, all}` where some unit declares a data allowance. `ipv6_count` counts units whose native IPv6 was checked through their own proxy port in the last 2 hours: what `require: ["ipv6"]` can buy (`p0f_ipv6_count` for `["p0f", "ipv6"]`). OpenVPN is guaranteed only on a buy with a `region_id` whose row has `openvpn_count == count` (no buy flag selects it); an order with `autoRenew: true` never gets a one-time unit (at most `count - one_time_only_count` per row, else 409 `auto_renew_unavailable` before any charge, subject to stock at order time). Counts are not a reservation: re-read right before checkout. Details: https://github.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/blob/main/docs/stock-and-credentials.md#guaranteeing-features-per-region
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/buy-modems-with-crypto-balance` - buy proxies. Body: `{tariff_id, modemCount, metadata}`. It is `modemCount`, NOT `modem_count`. Country/carrier come from the tariff; `region_id` pins a region. Only dedicated-line plans are accepted: a pool plan id answers `400 not_a_modem_tariff` (nothing charged). Optional `require`: `["p0f"]`, `["ipv6"]` or `["p0f", "ipv6"]`. Too few p0f units = `409 p0f_unavailable`; too few IPv6 units (with or without p0f) = `409 ipv6_unavailable`; other values = `400 unknown_requirement` with `supported: ["p0f", "ipv6"]`; nothing charged in each case. Guide: https://github.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/blob/main/docs/ipv6-lines.md
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/buy-with-account-credit` - buy with USD credit
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renewal-quote` - read-only exact renewal quote. Show any `warnings[].message` from the renewal quote before the customer confirms. `NODE_LINE_NOT_SERVING` means the line has been observed down for at least 24 hours. The customer can still renew.
- For an owned Node line advertising `proxyEndpoints.capabilities.autoRenew`, read `GET /modems/{id}/auto-renewal?days=30` and show the offer. With explicit approval send `PUT /modems/{id}/auto-renewal` with `{mode:"balance", autoRenewConsent:true, days:offer.days, expected_price_usd:offer.price_usd}`. Disable with `{mode:"off"}`. A one-time checkout does not enrol the line.
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renew-with-account-credit` - explicit renewal with USD credit (a line whose plan is not a dedicated-line plan answers `409 modem_tariff_invalid`: contact support)
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renew-modems-with-crypto-balance` - explicit renewal with BTC balance
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/restart` - rotate IP. Classic proxy: SYNCHRONOUS, `200` with `{result, rotated, ip, message}` - `rotated:false` is a failure returned as 200. There is no `?sync=true`, no `new_ip`, no 503. Within 60 s of the previous rotation (started or finished, failed included) it answers `429` with `code` `rotation_too_soon` or `rotation_cooldown`, a `Retry-After` header and the same `retry_after_seconds`. A row with `proxyEndpoints` answers `202` with `pending: true`: poll `GET /modems/{id}/rotation-status` until `done` or `failed`. A refusal there changes nothing. Coronium Node rows: `409` `modem_rotation_in_progress` (poll), `rotate_unavailable` (read `suggested_action`), `rental_conflict` (refresh the list). Other rows with `proxyEndpoints` can also answer `429 rotation_too_soon` with `Retry-After` (wait, retry once), `409 modem_expired` (renew first), `409 rotate_unavailable` + `check_proxy_health` (offline, do not loop) and `502 rotation_unconfirmed` (submitted: poll rotation-status, do not resend). On a Node row, `proxyEndpoints.rotationState` can be `busy`, `needs_review` or null. A `409 rotate_unavailable` with `suggested_action: retry_later` means the previous IP change is still being confirmed. Refresh status after a minute and keep new rotation requests paused until the hold clears.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/rotate-modem-by-token/{token}` - token-auth rotation. Classic proxy: `200` only on a verified new IP (`ext_ip`/`new_ip`), `502` otherwise (branch on the HTTP status, not on a body error code), `429` during the ~60 s per-modem cooldown. On a line with `proxyEndpoints` the token URL answers `202` with `{pending: true, status_url}`. Follow `status_url` as returned until it settles, and do not resend: every call is a new request. `status_url` may be on a neutral short-link host (for example `https://ipreset.xyz/s/<token>`): same `data` shape, but errors there carry only `error` (no envelope `code`), so branch on the HTTP status, or poll `GET /api/v3/modems/get-rotating-modem-status-by-token/{token}` with the same token for envelope codes. On a Coronium Node row refusals are `409` whose `code` usually reads `modem_rotation_in_progress` / `poll_rotation_status` whatever the reason (an ended rental can read `internal_error`), so decide from `error`: a rotation already in progress, too soon, a previous change still being confirmed (refresh status later), or an active rental required (reload the proxy list). On other rows with `proxyEndpoints` the codes are real: `429 rotation_too_soon` (wait `Retry-After`), `409 modem_expired` / `rotate_unavailable` / `modem_rotation_in_progress`, and `502 rotation_unconfirmed` (submitted: poll `status_url`, do not resend). `503` means rotation is unavailable right now; do not poll.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/get-rotating-modem-status-by-token/{token}` - no-auth status of the last rotation, same token. Coronium Node row: poll `data.rotation` until `pending` is false (`success: true` = done, `needs_review: true` = still being confirmed: refresh status later, anything else = failed). Other rows with `proxyEndpoints`: read `data.state` (`done` or `failed`). Classic row: only `data.status`, `ext_ip`, `rotated_at`.
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/set-rotation-interval`. Use seconds for `rotation_interval`. Zero disables a timer. For a Node line, use the bounds returned in `proxyEndpoints.rotationSchedule` (120 to 86400 in steps of 60) when `capabilities.rotationInterval` is true. A stored schedule can still be turned off. Other timed rows with `proxyEndpoints` accept 60 to 2592000 in steps of 60. Classic rows accept 60 or more.
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/replace` - swap broken proxy; remaining time and `metadata` are kept. A p0f line gets a p0f line or `409 p0f_replacement_unavailable` (nothing changed); body `{"allow_without_p0f": true}` accepts one without p0f. A line bought with `require: ["ipv6"]` gets a line with a fresh IPv6 check (`ipv6: {required: true, kept: true}`) or `409 ipv6_replacement_unavailable` (nothing changed); `{"allow_without_ipv6": true}` accepts one without IPv6. No replacement in stock = `400 "No free modems!"` (not 409 no_stock, branch on status + message); daily limit = 400; failed delivery = 500 with the current proxy unchanged and no late second line; a concurrent call = `409 request_in_progress`; lines that cannot be replaced through the API = `409` (code `action_unsupported`, or `internal_error` with an error that says to contact support); a move already running = `409` "being moved right now" (refetch in a few minutes); `500` "needs a check by support" = nothing charged, do not retry. A proxy you already replaced answers `409 already_replaced` (`suggested_action` `use_current_modem`) with `current_modem` `{_id, name}` (null when that proxy left your account); nothing changes. A moved line answers `moved: true` with `newModemId` equal to `oldModemId`: same login, password and expiry, ports may change, and your own `/replace` sends no event if the ports stayed the same. Do not rely on `IMEI`/`portId` (deprecated, removed 2026-11-19); refetch the line.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/p0f-options` / `PUT .../set-os` `{"os": "<value>"}` - OS fingerprint. Lines carry `features.p0f.{server_supported, supported_values, vocabulary, unavailable_reason}`; there is no `features.p0f.provider`. `200` = applied (`data.applied: true`, or `data.noop: true` when the line already had that value); `202` with `data.pending: true` = sent, not yet confirmed (do not resend, read `p0f_os` later; optional UUIDv4 `request_id` makes a retry safe). Refusals: `400 p0f_unsupported_on_server`, `400 p0f_os_unsupported_on_this_server`, `429` (one change per 5 min), `502 p0f_not_applied`, `404 p0f_unavailable` (contact support). Some lines use `400 p0f_os_not_supported_on_server`, `429 p0f_rate_limited`, `409 p0f_change_in_progress`, `409 p0f_proxy_offline`, `409 rental_conflict`, `400 invalid_request`; branch on the HTTP status first.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/openvpn` - `.ovpn` profile. `503 openvpn_profile_pending` + `Retry-After` on a line set up in the last 2 h: retry the same line, never replace. `409 openvpn_not_supported` / `400 openvpn_disabled` are final; check the line's `features.openvpn.available`.
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/set-metadata` - replace the complete metadata field on an owned modem; verify the receipt and current mapping before repairing missing metadata, then read back the result
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/usage` - per-day data use, only where `proxyEndpoints.capabilities.usage` is true
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/history` - cursor-paginated change log of your proxies and account (`{data, next_cursor, partial, live_since}`), the polling counterpart of the `history_events` webhooks
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/payments` - payment ledger, for reconciliation
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/subscriptions` - auto-renew state per proxy
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/webhook` - register webhook URL (a public `https://` host; private, internal or non-resolving hosts answer `400 invalid_webhook_target`; redirects are never followed)
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/webhook/test` - fire a real signed test event; returns `delivered`, `status_code`, `latency_ms` and, on failure, a short `error` plus `error_code` (`invalid_url`, `refused_target`, `dns_failed`, `timeout`, `tls_error`, `connection_failed`). `response_preview` is always null: your endpoint's body is never echoed

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header. Integrations use the account API key (Dashboard -> Account -> API Access): it needs no two-factor code, is not ended by a password change, and authenticates its own request only (it never creates a dashboard session). Dashboard API key lifetime 365 days; regenerate it in Dashboard -> Account -> API Access (this revokes the old one). Only a `401` with `code` `auth_required` is a key problem: on the BTC lane (`/payment/buy-modems-with-crypto-balance`, `/payment/renew-modems-with-crypto-balance`) `401 "Insufficient crypto balance"` (`code` `internal_error`, `required`/`available` in BTC) means the BTC balance is too low, so fund it and never regenerate the key. `/get-token` and `/signup` never reveal whether an account exists (`401 Invalid email or password.` for both unknown address and wrong password). No account yet: an agent can sign up and get the key through the API (see the signup line above). `POST /get-token` on a two-factor account without `code` answers `401` with `code` `two_factor_required`; login tokens from it end when the password or two-factor setting changes or on "log out everywhere". `/api/v1/create-token` is retired (`410`).

The starter dashboard uses the reseller’s existing Coronium funds. Keep on-chain deposits under the account owner’s control. Account credit (USD) is added in the dashboard and spent by `/payment/buy-with-account-credit`. USDT (TRC-20) and BTC go to the deposit addresses from `GET /account/crypto-balance` (an array; the entries with `coin: "usdt"` and `coin: "btc"` have `address` and `balance`), sent from the person's own wallet. Once a deposit confirms, `POST /account/balance/convert` moves it into USD account credit, one way (preview with `dry_run: true`, then the real move with the person's yes and an `Idempotency-Key` of 8-128 letters, digits, `-` or `_`). A BTC balance can also pay directly on `/payment/buy-modems-with-crypto-balance`, which converts the USD total to BTC at order time; larger orders wait until the deposit is mined. A saved card pays on `/payment/buy-with-card/{card_id}`. Read `GET /account` before each buy to see which balance can pay. Refunds go back to the Coronium balance. The paid 24-hour plan is the way to test a line.

Errors on `/api/v3` return `{error, code, reason_code?, suggested_action, retryable, request_id}` plus an `X-Request-Id` header. `error` is the human string, `code` the machine id. There is no `message` field.

## Critical patterns

- **Customer mapping**: send `metadata` as an object or a string. Objects are JSON-serialized; string inputs are preserved. Proxy lists return the stored string, which need not contain JSON. Keep an order/payment/modem-to-customer index and signed webhook inbox. Replacements keep metadata. Missing/null metadata alone is not failed delivery: reconcile receipts and current ownership, never re-buy or replay an old payment to recover it. A setter replaces the whole value, so preserve intended keys and stop on a conflicting current mapping; an already-delivered retry must not reset later edits.
- **Server-side JWT**: never put `CORONIUM_API_KEY` in client-side code. All API calls go through the reseller's own server.
- **Webhook replacements**: `modem.replaced` is sent for every replacement that changes the connection details (automatic when a modem dies, your own `POST /modems/:id/replace`, or support) and the new proxy keeps your `metadata`. Fields are nested under `data` (`data.old_modem_id`, `data.new_modem_id`, `data.new_modem`), the envelope carries `event_id`/`occurred_at`/`account`. Key on `data.new_modem_id` (always set) and refetch the line before handing out credentials: `new_modem` uses `_id`/`proxy_login`/`proxy_password`/`tariff_expired_at` on a classic replace or automatic swap (also when the automatic swap moved the line), and `id`/`login`/`password`/`expires_at` on a replacement by support or the notice for a moved line whose ports changed. The automatic swap (8 failed checks, HTTPS webhook, more than 24 h left) sends the event (`new_modem_id` equal to `old_modem_id` when it moved the line), twice when the ports changed; dedupe. Some lines are also moved automatically after about 30 minutes offline with no webhook required: that move keeps the credentials and sends `modem.replaced` only when the ports changed, in the `id`/`login` shape only. A move that keeps the same ports sends none. Every move writes `proxy.moved` to `GET /account/history`; poll it (or `GET /account/proxies`) if you have no webhook. Deliveries are HMAC-signed (`X-Coronium-Signature`) and retried up to 8 times.
- **Idempotency**: `Idempotency-Key` header on the starter dashboard’s purchase and renewal requests and on a real `/account/balance/convert` move (required there), `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}`, 24h replay window. One key per buy intent, reused across retries. `409 duplicate_request` (`new_order_created: false`) carries `reason` (`idempotency_key_conflict`, `recent_identical_request`, `request_in_progress`, `request_outcome_unknown`): no order was created by that request; check `/account/payments` and `/account/proxies`, do not switch to a new key to get past it.
- **Approved price**: send `max_total_usd` (the total the buyer approved, in USD) on the starter dashboard’s buys and renewals; for renewals take `total_usd` from `/payment/renewal-quote`. Above it the API answers `409 price_changed` with a fresh `quote` and charges nothing: show it and ask again. Other payment refusals: `400 insufficient_balance` (account credit too low, nothing charged), `409 renewal_already_pending` on account-credit renewals (already paid, still applying: do not retry) and `429 renewal_burst` (3 renewals in 10 minutes: wait). `429 payment_in_progress`: another payment on this account is running, nothing charged; wait `Retry-After` (5 s) and resend with the SAME `Idempotency-Key`. `202` with `paymentId`, or `503 payment_delivery_unconfirmed` with `paymentId`: the balance was debited; follow `GET /payments/{paymentId}/status` and never re-order with a new key. `503 no_stock` / `upstream_degraded` with `refunded: true`: the charge was returned to the balance at once, a new order is safe. `409 node_renewal_reconciling` on a renewal: refresh the proxy list, do not repeat the renewal.
- **Stock header (optional)**: Units with one login on both ports are offered without any header. `X-Coronium-Proxy-Credentials: separate-protocol-v1` on stock and purchase calls also offers units with separate HTTP/SOCKS5 logins; then read `proxyEndpoints.http` and `.socks5` and never reuse HTTP credentials for SOCKS5.
- **Capabilities, not provider**: `proxyEndpoints.provider` is an opaque label - never branch on it or show it. The one documented value is `coronium_node` (Coronium Node rows). Use `proxyEndpoints.capabilities` to decide which actions exist for a proxy.
- **Coupons**: add `"coupon": {"coupon_name": "CODE"}` to the body of `/payment/buy-with-account-credit`, `/payment/buy-modems-with-crypto-balance`, the two renew routes and `/payment/renewal-quote`. Check the code once with `POST /coupons/check` `{"coupon_name": "CODE"}` (`coupon_name` a string of at most 64 characters, else `400`): `200 {data: {discount: "15%"}}` (every coupon is a percentage; `discount: 0` means this account already used it); an unknown, expired, revoked or not-applicable code answers `404` with one message, "This coupon code is not valid for your account." Branch on the status, not on `code`. Checks are limited (120 per 10 minutes per account and per IP address; 10 misses a day per account, 30 per network, then `429` with `Retry-After`), so cache a validated code for the session instead of checking it before every order. A buy with a code that no longer applies does not fail, it is priced at list price, so send the discounted total as `max_total_usd`: then a dropped coupon answers `409 price_changed` and charges nothing. Read the applied discount from `billing.discount`; list price is `billing.subtotal_usd`.

## Limits and error answers (live since 13 Nov 2026)

- **Malformed input answers 400, not 500.** A malformed payment, ticket or pool id in the path, a value of the wrong type, invalid JSON, or a body or query key that starts with `$` answers `400` with `BAD_PARAMETERS` in `code` or `reason_code` (on `/api/v3` routes the envelope `code` is `invalid_request`). Fix the request; do not retry it unchanged.
- **`429` means wait.** Every limit answers `429` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds) and `retry_after_seconds` in the body. Wait that long; do not retry sooner or rotate keys or addresses.
- **Sign-in**: `POST /get-token` is limited per IP address (5 requests in 10 s, 15 a minute, 60 an hour). 10 failed sign-ins for one account from one network in 15 minutes block that pair for 15 minutes; 30 failed sign-ins from one IP address in an hour block it for an hour. A missing two-factor code counts as a failure. Use the API key instead of signing in repeatedly.
- **Profile fields**: `name` at most 80 characters, `company_name` 120, `purpose` 500 (sign-up included). `name` and `company_name` may not contain `<` or `>`. Longer or invalid values answer `400`; nothing is cut.
- **Hosted MCP**: OAuth connections to `https://api.coronium.io/mcp` and `/mcp/buyer` end when the account password or two-factor setting changes or on "log out everywhere". Connect again.
- Offer IP whitelisting only when the owned row advertises `proxyEndpoints.capabilities.whitelist: true` or `features.whitelist.available: true`. When both are absent or false, hide the control and use the line’s login and password.

## Don't

- Don't reinvent auto-swap or health-check logic - the backend does it.
- Don't put JWT in browser.
- Don't call `POST /coupons/check` before every order; validate a code once and cache it.
- Don't automate `POST /get-token` with a password; use the account API key.
- Don't treat a 200 from `/restart` as a successful rotation - check `rotated`.
- Don't read webhook fields off the top level - they are under `data`.
- Don't document or depend on `proxy.expiring_soon`; the API advertises it but it never fires.
- Don't retry-loop on `409 no_stock` (`reason_code: OUT_OF_STOCK`). Ask the buyer to choose another available product.
